error.unreachableBody: The dashboard could not reach the bot.
error.botLeftTitle: Testify is not in that server
error.botLeftBody: Invite it back and this page will work again.
error.cannotManageBody: You need the Manage Server permission there.
error.notAMemberTitle: You are not in that server
error.setupRequiredBody: Finish the setup steps on the sign-in page.

notFound.title: Page not found
notFound.subtitle: That address does not match any screen in this dashboard.
notFound.emptyBody: Check the address for a typo, or start again from your servers. If a link inside the dashboard brought you here, that is worth reporting.

help.title: Getting started
help.subtitle: What {{name}} does, how to set it up, and where everything lives.
help.inviteTitle: Add the bot to your server
help.inviteBody: {{name}} has to be in a server before there is anything to configure. The servers page marks the ones you can add it to.
help.pickBody: Everything you change applies to the one server you have open, and its name sits above every screen.
help.configureBody: Nothing is switched on by default. Open a section in the sidebar, turn it on, and it starts working straight away.
help.tellBody: Members use the bot in Discord rather than here. The command list says what each command does and what it takes.
help.slashDetail: Type a slash in any channel and Discord lists them, along with the options each one takes.
help.prefixDetail: The same commands, typed as ordinary text. The prefix is t? until you change it under Settings.
help.switchDetail: Any command can be turned off for one server, or for every server, without removing the bot.
help.tourSubtitle: The same list as the sidebar, with a line on each.
help.stuckBody: The support server is the quickest way to reach somebody, and the source is public if you would rather read it.

appearance.title: Appearance
appearance.subtitle: How this dashboard looks in your browser. Nobody else is affected.
appearance.themeDescribes: Follow the system and it changes when your device does, at sunset or on a schedule you already set.
appearance.systemHint: Match whatever this device is set to
appearance.alwaysLight: Always light, whatever the device is set to
appearance.alwaysDark: Always dark, whatever the device is set to
appearance.accentDescribes: The colour used for links, buttons and the focus ring. Green, amber and red keep their own meanings whatever you choose.
appearance.motionDescribes: Animation here is feedback rather than decoration, so turning it off costs you nothing.
appearance.motionSystemHint: Follow the reduced-motion setting on this device
appearance.motionFullHint: Animate, even where this device asks for less
appearance.motionReducedHint: Hold everything still, whatever the device asks for
appearance.languageDescribes: Testify’s own messages in Discord are not translated — this is the dashboard only.

guilds.title: Servers
guilds.subtitle: Everywhere you can change Testify’s settings, or add it.
guilds.emptyBody: You need Manage Server in a server before it shows up here. Ask its owner, or invite Testify to one of your own.
guilds.noMatchBody: Try part of the name instead.
guilds.noPermissionHint: Adding a bot needs the Manage Server permission. Ask somebody who has it.
guilds.configurableBody: Testify is in these, so every setting is one click away.
guilds.invitableBody: You have Manage Server here, so you can invite Testify yourself.
guilds.lockedBody: Adding a bot takes Manage Server, which you do not have in these.

overview.subtitle: What Testify is doing in this server.
overview.featuresHint: Features Testify is actively running here, out of everything it offers.
overview.nothingChangedBody: Every change made from this dashboard is recorded, so you can see who turned what off and when.
overview.missingBody: These features are configured but will quietly do nothing until Testify is granted them.

automod.title: AutoMod
automod.subtitle: Discord’s own message filters. Testify sets them up; Discord enforces them.
automod.mentionsHint: A message with more is blocked.
automod.addOneBelow: Add one below, and Discord blocks matching messages before anyone reads them.
automod.needsPermission: Grant Testify the Manage Server permission to see this server’s rules.
automod.needsManageServer: Testify needs the Manage Server permission before it can read or change AutoMod rules in this server.
automod.limitsBody: Discord allows a handful of each kind. It refuses the rest, and this says so when it does.

auth.envBody: The dashboard is switched on but cannot sign anybody in yet. Add these to your .env and restart the bot:
auth.secretBody: Run npm run secret -- --write to generate that one.
auth.redirectBody: Then add this under OAuth2 → Redirects in the Discord Developer Portal:
auth.configureBody: Configure {{name}} in any server where you have Manage Server, without opening Discord.
auth.cancelled: You cancelled the Discord sign-in. Nothing was shared.
auth.scopes: {{name}} asks for <scope>identify</scope> to know who you are and <scope>guilds</scope> to list your servers. It never asks for your email, and it cannot read your messages through this.
auth.agree: By signing in you agree to the <terms>terms of use</terms>. What {{name}} stores is set out in the <privacy>privacy notice</privacy>.
auth.title: Sign in

auditLog.title: Audit logging
auditLog.subtitle: Which server events Testify records, and where it posts them.
auditLog.whereBody: One channel receives every event chosen below.
auditLog.recordHint: Off removes the configuration entirely. Nothing already posted is deleted.
auditLog.postToHint: Somewhere only moderators can read — an audit log names who did what.
auditLog.whatBody: Tick a heading to take the whole group.
auditLog.allSelected: Everything is selected, so events added in a future update are logged too.

treasure.title: Treasure drops
treasure.subtitle: Testify drops money into chat now and then, for whoever claims it first.
treasure.cooldownHint: Minutes before another drop can appear, however busy the chat is.
treasure.notSetUpYet: Not set up yet — the numbers below are the defaults until you turn drops on.
treasure.howBody: Testify picks a number in each range, so drops do not land on a predictable beat.

welcome.title: Welcome messages
welcome.subtitle: What Testify says when somebody joins, and where.
welcome.sendToHint: Everything below is stored against this channel, so it has to be chosen first.
welcome.pickFirst: Pick a channel and the rest of this page turns on.
welcome.greetHint: Off means Testify says nothing when somebody joins. The message is kept.
welcome.tooLong: That message is longer than Discord will accept. Shorten it before saving.

sticky.title: Sticky messages
sticky.subtitle: A message Testify reposts to keep it at the bottom of a busy channel.
sticky.emptyBody: Pick a channel below and Testify will keep a message pinned to the bottom of it.
sticky.addBody: One per channel. Editing an existing one is done above.
sticky.channelHint: Testify needs permission to post here, or the sticky will never appear.
sticky.repostHint: How many messages pass before Testify posts it again.
sticky.full: That is the most stickies Testify can hold. Remove one to add another.

commands.title: Commands
commands.onDashboardHint: Commands with a settings screen here. The rest are still Discord-only.
commands.searchPlaceholder: Search by name, alias or description
commands.noMatchBody: Try part of a name, an alias like ban, or clear the category filter.
commands.switchRefused: That switch could not be saved.
commands.subtitleGlobal: Everything Testify can do. A command switched off here is off in every server, for everybody.
commands.subtitleGuild: Everything Testify can do. Switch one off and nobody in this server can run it, either way.
commands.subtitlePlain: Everything Testify can do, on both the slash and prefix surfaces.
commands.availableToAll: Anybody who may use it can run it
commands.offHere: Nobody in this server can run it
commands.offEverywhere: The bot owner switched this off everywhere
commands.locked: Testify needs this one to stay on

giveaways.title: Giveaways
giveaways.subtitle: Start one, end it early, or draw again — without reading a message ID out of Discord.
giveaways.emptyBody: Start one above and it appears here, with the controls to end or redraw it.
giveaways.startBody: Testify posts it and draws the winners when the time is up. Members enter with the 🎉 reaction.

levelling.title: Levelling
levelling.subtitle: Who earns XP, what they get for it, and where it is announced.
levelling.earnXpHint: Turning this off stops XP being awarded. Nobody loses what they already earned.
levelling.stackHint: Off means only the highest reward role is kept as members level past each tier.
levelling.rewardsFull: That is the most rewards Testify can hold. Remove one to add another.
levelling.hierarchyNote: Roles above Testify in the hierarchy are hidden, because it could not grant them.
levelling.ignoresBody: Nothing said here, or by anyone holding these roles, earns XP.
levelling.boostsBody: Members holding one of these earn more XP. Someone with several gets the highest, not the product.

members.title: Members
members.subtitle: Who is ahead on money and on levels. Both boards are the same ones Discord’s /leaderboard shows.
members.issueHint: They are not notified from here.
members.deleteWarning: This deletes the whole record. It cannot be undone.
members.levelOrXp: Set a level or change the XP, not both at once.
members.noXpYet: They have earned no XP here yet.
members.noAccountYet: They have no account here yet — adding money opens one.
members.levelRewardNote: Any role rewards the new level earns are handed out at the same time.

tickets.title: Tickets
tickets.subtitle: A button members press to open a private channel with your staff.
tickets.whereBody: All four are needed before the panel can be posted.
tickets.categoryHint: New ticket channels are created under this.
tickets.transcriptsHint: Where a closed ticket’s transcript is sent.
tickets.staffRoleHint: The role that can see and handle every ticket.
tickets.postAgain: Posting again edits the panel already out there rather than leaving a second one.
tickets.nothingPosted: Nothing is posted until you press the button below.
tickets.turnOffBody: Open ticket channels are left alone. The panel message has to be deleted by hand.

lottery.title: Lottery
lottery.subtitle: A pot members buy tickets into, drawn on a schedule.
lottery.noDrawsBody: The first one appears here once it runs.
lottery.howBody: Members buy tickets with <command>/lottery enter</command>. Every ticket adds its fee to the pot.

settings.title: Server settings
settings.subtitle: The switches that do not have a screen of their own.
settings.countingBody: One channel where members count upwards, one number each.
settings.countingRunHint: Off removes the configuration. The count is not kept.
settings.autoRoleBody: Given to everybody who joins, as soon as they arrive.
settings.voiceBody: Voice channels renamed to show how many members and bots the server has.
settings.prefixBody: What people type before a command name. Slash commands are unaffected by anything here.
settings.prefixAllowHint: Off means only slash commands work in this server.
settings.linkBody: Deletes links posted by anybody without the bypass permission.
settings.linkDeleteHint: Testify needs Manage Messages in the channel for this to work.
settings.linkBypassHint: Anybody with this permission is never filtered.
settings.nickBody: A nickname for this server only. The picture is the same everywhere and only the bot owner can change it.
settings.nickNeedsPermission: Testify needs the Change Nickname permission in this server before it can be renamed.
settings.verifyBody: A button new members press to prove they are there, and the role it hands them.
settings.verifyOnHint: Off removes the configuration. The panel already posted stops working.
settings.verifyInHint: A channel new members can see before they have the role.
settings.roleTooHigh: That role sits at or above Testify’s own, so Testify cannot give it to anybody. Move Testify’s role higher in Server Settings → Roles, or pick a lower one.

owner.title: Owner console
owner.subtitle: How Testify is running, and what it is being used for.
owner.membersHint: Everyone Testify can see, counted across every server. People in two servers count twice.
owner.uptimeHint: Since the bot process last started, not since it last connected to Discord.
owner.mostUsedHint: Where the work goes, and where a regression would hurt most.
owner.leastUsedHint: Counted over every command the bot has, so a command nobody runs shows as zero.
owner.busiestHint: Ranked by commands run, not by how many members they have.
owner.howRunHint: Whether the prefix is still worth maintaining.
owner.screensHint: Counted bot-wide by route, with no server or account attached — see the privacy notice.
owner.nothingLoggedBody: Nothing at this level since the bot last started.
owner.nobodyBlockedBody: Anyone blocked here is refused before a command runs, in every server.
owner.nothingRunBody: Pick a command above. Its reply appears here rather than in a Discord channel.
owner.discordOnly: Part of this reply only works inside Discord. Run it there to use the controls it offered.
owner.stopping: Testify is stopping. This page will stop responding in a moment.
owner.guildTableCaption: Servers Testify is in, largest first
owner.pausedBody: Testify is connected but refusing everything. No commands, no XP, no automod.
owner.noCommandRun: No command has been run yet.
owner.noServerRun: No server has run a command yet.
owner.noScreenOpened: No screen has been opened yet.
owner.couldNotShutDown: Testify could not be shut down.
owner.leaveBody: Testify stops answering there immediately. Getting back in needs a fresh invite from someone still inside, and its settings are kept in case it returns.
owner.blacklistBody: A blocked account cannot run any command, on either surface, in any server. Bot-wide — to stop one command in one server, switch it off instead.
owner.idShape: A user ID is 17 to 20 digits.
owner.identityBody: The bot’s global profile, in every server at once. Discord has no per-server picture for bots — a manager gets a nickname and nothing more.
owner.renameLimit: Discord allows two username changes an hour and refuses the rest — the message below is Discord’s, not Testify’s.
owner.shutDownBody: Stops the whole process, and this dashboard with it — the bot serves it. Only your host can start it again: systemd, Docker or a terminal.
owner.levelFloor: Testify is running at <level>{{level}}</level>, so nothing below that is written at all. Restart it with a lower level to capture more.
owner.redactedNote: Anything that looked like a token, a password or a connection string was removed before the line was stored.
owner.runnerBody: Runs here rather than in a server: nothing is posted to Discord, and the reply comes back below. Only read-only owner commands are listed.
owner.versionBody: You are running <version>v{{version}}</version>. Testify never contacts a server to check for a newer one — a self-hosted bot that phones home on a timer is not something to ship by default. Compare it against the releases page when you want to.
owner.blockListFailed: The block list could not be loaded, so this is not a list of who is blocked.

legal.englishGoverns: Translated for convenience. Where a translation and the English text disagree, the English text is the one that governs.
legal.termsSummary: Testify is open-source software you or somebody you know is running. These terms cover using this instance of it.
legal.whoRunsP1: Testify is self-hosted. Whoever deployed this instance — the operator — decides what it does, what it stores and who can reach it. They are responsible for it, not the project’s authors.
legal.whoRunsP2: The software is provided as-is, without warranty of any kind. Nobody promises it will be available, correct, or free of defects.
legal.usingBotP1: By adding Testify to a server or using its commands you agree to the following.
legal.usingBotL1: Follow Discord’s Terms of Service and Community Guidelines. Nothing here overrides them.
legal.usingBotL2: Do not use the bot to harass anybody, to break the law, or to evade a moderation action.
legal.usingBotL3: Do not try to break, overload or extract data from the bot or the machine it runs on.
legal.usingBotL4: A server’s moderators, not the bot, are responsible for what happens in that server.
legal.usingDashboardP1: You can only configure a server you already have Manage Server in. That permission is checked live on every request, so losing it takes effect immediately.
legal.usingDashboardP2: Every change made here is written to an audit log with your Discord account attached, so the server’s other managers can see who changed what.
legal.inBot: Economy, levels and other in-bot things
legal.inBotP1: Coins, levels, items and anything else the bot tracks have no monetary value, cannot be exchanged for anything, and may be reset at any time by a server’s moderators or by the operator.
legal.endingP1: You can stop using Testify at any time by removing it from your server. When it is removed, the settings it stored for that server are deleted.
legal.endingP2: The operator may remove the bot from a server, or block an account from using it, at their discretion.
legal.changesP1: These terms may change as the software does. The current text is always the one on this page, and the project’s history is public.
legal.privacySummary: What Testify stores, why, and for how long. It is a short list on purpose — the bot collects the minimum it needs to work.
legal.storedP1: Testify keeps only what a feature needs to function.
legal.storedL1: Server settings: the prefix, which features are on, which channels and roles they use.
legal.storedL2: Per-server, per-member records for features you turn on: levels and XP, economy balances and items, warnings, and verification status.
legal.storedL3: A dashboard session when you sign in: your Discord user id, your username, and your OAuth tokens, encrypted at rest.
legal.storedL4: An audit record for every change made from the dashboard: who made it, what changed, and when.
legal.storedL5: Command usage counts: which command, in which server, on which day. No user ids are stored with these.
legal.storedL6: Dashboard screen counts: which screen was opened and on which day. Counted bot-wide — no user id and no server id is stored with these, so they say which screens get used and nothing about who used them.
legal.notStoredP1: Testify does not read or keep your message history. Message content is processed in memory for features you enable — automod, counting, XP — and is never written to the database.
legal.notStoredP2: Your Discord password and email are never seen by this bot: signing in goes through Discord’s own OAuth, and Testify only receives your id, username, avatar and the servers you are in.
legal.notStoredP3: The bot does not sell, share or transmit anything to a third party. It talks to Discord and to its own database, and nothing else.
legal.logConsoleP1: The operator can see the bot’s recent log lines from the owner console. Anything that looks like a token, password or connection string is removed before a line is stored, and the buffer holds only the last few hundred lines in memory — a restart clears it.
legal.retentionP1: Nothing is kept longer than it is useful.
legal.retentionL1: Server settings: until the bot is removed from that server, then deleted.
legal.retentionL2: Dashboard sessions: expire on their own, and signing out deletes them immediately.
legal.retentionL3: Audit records and usage counts: 90 days, then deleted automatically.
legal.retentionL4: Levels, balances and other member records: until the server’s moderators reset them, or the bot is removed.
legal.removalP1: Removing the bot from a server deletes that server’s settings. For anything about you personally, ask the operator of this instance — they run the database and can delete it.
legal.cookiesP1: One cookie, set when you sign in, holding a signed session identifier. It is httpOnly, same-site, and marked Secure when the dashboard is served over HTTPS. There is no third-party cookie, no advertising identifier, and nothing that follows you between sites. Your IP address is not stored, and neither is your location, your browser or your device.
